questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture and place. I didn’t want to be too far away from home but I did want to experience another culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not too difficult but also not that easy. A lot of us exchange students were extremely confused and the administration system at the University of Edinburgh is a bit of a mess

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of letters and was a part of a Facebook group for exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It’s very confusing and everything was kind of scattered across the different university buildings and it is easy to get lost in Edinburgh

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was extremely time consuming and difficult because of the short period of time that I needed an apartment. 
I would suggest calling the different letting agencies and tell them what you need, they are very kind and helpful and will guide you.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It’s extremely expensive! 
You also have to pay council tax which is expensive BUT you can get a student discount even though that can be a bit of a mess as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of my friends whom I met in Edinburgh weren’t able to get housing by the University and had to apply at Napier University’s housing instead (which they got), unless you’re staying a whole year then I would recommend doing that or finding private housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Oof. I can barely remember. There are a lot of link and pamphlets etc that you get once you’ve been accepted, so you just have to click on them and then that should lead you to what you need.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Pamphlets, Facebook Groups and e-mails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very! I got the classes I wanted, though the archaeology class I got was not my first choice but I still enjoyed it very much and I can highly recommend Introduction to Gaelic language and culture as well as Celtic Civilisations 1A (both belong to the school of linguistics). You learn a lot about Scotland as well as its place in the world

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Patience and deep breaths. A lot of coffee

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had two first year courses and one third year course. There was a clear difference between them but that weren’t that difficult. Though be prepared for the amount of assignments and quizzes etc. 
at the start it was really intense because of the speed in which the classes were going. You get a lot of knowledge in 1-2 hours and they are speaking very fast.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Hmm. It was a lot of seminars and lectures, every Friday we had workshops in smaller group were we discussed topics. A lot like KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bronze Age Civilisations in the Near East and Greece

Introduction to Gaelic Language and Culture

Celtic Civilisations 1A

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the Celtic and Gaelic ones! They were amazing and so exciting especially because you learn a lot about Scotland’s culture, history and traditions.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn’t have any unexpected costs other than me being an impulsive buyer and had to buy an extra suitcase for my flight home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is surprisingly cheap, as well as Books and public transportation (which I only used a couple of times). A lot of the museums are free but the tourist attractions such as Mary King’s Close and Edinburgh castle are expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were Pub Crawls, Karaoke Nights, Ceilidhs and a lot of trips for Exchange students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think I most enjoyed walking around Old Town as well as Edinburgh’s Christmas Market, they are both free (except for all the stuff you can buy in the stores) and it is the best way to experience the culture.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Exploring the city! Hiking Arthur’s Seat, seeing Carlton Hill, and I would suggest joining a University Community such as The Occult Club (it’s a vibe). I’d also suggest getting a tattoo (I did!).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. In the end it’s a European citadel it’s not that different except for the Pipers stationed in Old Town.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The week before semester start is a golden opportunity otherwise don’t be afraid to talk to people in class, they tend to be really nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Bagpiping and the Gaelic language it’s uniquely ‘Scottish’ and it’s amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Choose a course based on what you find interesting (does not necessarily have to do anything with you actual class/education)

2. Take the bus from the airport when you arrive, it’s not too expensive.

3. Just enjoy it! Do what you think sounds fun and interesting! Don’t worry too much about the grades (as long as you pass the class nothing else matter).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It’s your trip, what is my experience does not have to be yours. Do what you feel is right.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The trip itself was so rewarding and just knowing that you can do this on your own is such a rewarding accomplishment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My anxiety can give me difficulties with social interaction, and the amount of people in Edinburgh can be a bit overwhelming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You, as a pedestrian, are allowed to cross the road even if the light is red.. people can actually get a bit annoyed if you don’t…

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
